2.why: False in the IDOR sense: a token only ever resets the account it was issued for (record.accountKey is used, never user input), though any session possessing the token may confirm it.

3.why: True: replacePassword updates account.passwordHash but never invalidates other entries in the sessions map, so previously authenticated sessions remain valid until their 8-hour expiry.

5.why: Passwords are hashed with Argon2id and reset tokens/identity codes are stored only as SHA-256 digests, which are appropriate algorithms (hashing rather than encryption), though MFA codes sit unhashed in the session.

6.why: There is no real email; the mock delivery returns the token in the JSON response and a URL query parameter and prints it in the page logs, though no other PII is included and Referrer-Policy is no-referrer.

7.why: All user inputs (identifier, token, identity value, passwords, MFA codes) pass strict allowlist regex validation, request bodies are size-bounded at 8KB, and the client renders all data via textContent.

8.why: renderLink only constructs same-origin links with pathname '/', a recovery-test parameter and no hash, rejecting protocol-relative URLs, and the server itself issues no redirects.

9.why: Mock delivery and log messages are inserted exclusively via textContent and a strict nonce-based CSP forbids inline scripts, so no user-supplied HTML or script can be rendered.

12.why: False: provision() creates three accounts (helena@example.com, etc.) all sharing the same hardcoded initial password, which function as usable default credentials.

13.why: Login, token confirmation, identity verification, MFA code and possession checks each impose a 5-minute lockout after 5 failures, and recovery issuance is rate-limited to 3 per 15 minutes per session/account.
